messages:
liz: heads up — hit a manifestless shard in staging, loader failed to resolve and hotpatch path didn't kick in. reproducer attached in thread but short summary: safetensors file present, no accompanying manifest, loader threw UnknownManifestError and we timed out the warmup.

sam: by manifestless you mean the .index/.json that our indexer usually emits is missing? any quick hex dump of the header?

liz: right — file starts with safetensors magic but the index blob we expect is absent. header looks like this (copied from the file head):
```json
{"magic":"safetensors","version":"1","meta":{}}
```
no shard map, no byte ranges. we only discovered after a partial warmup failed.

ankur: hmm. two orthogonal problems: loader needs a resolver/negotiation layer that can deal with missing manifests, and the warmup flow needs a safe fallback that doesn't assume full manifest. otherwise callers see big cold latency.

maria: agree on both. options: 1) conservative: refuse to serve manifestless (fail fast) 2) scan file to build a manifest on the fly (expensive) 3) ask a remote manifest service (if available) or 4) heuristic lazy-warmup + background manifest build. each has tradeoffs.

sam: +1 for a resolver plugin interface so infra teams can plug DB lookup vs on-disk scan. proposed minimal API: `Resolver.resolve(path) -> manifest | null` and `Resolver.priority` ordering.

ankur: sketch of fallback order i proposed in thread:
```yaml
weights_resolver:
  order: [manifest-db, inline-index, scan-heuristics, fail]
  scan-heuristics:
    max_scan_bytes: 64MB
    try_safetensors_footer: true
```
That lets us pick low-cost options first.

liz: we also need a warmup contract so runtime can start with partial info. proposal: if manifest missing, do a tiny prefix KV warmup (first 4MB), start the model, then background-resolve full shard and apply "hotpatch" replacing pages/chunks when available. pseudo: 
```py
if not manifest:
  prefetch(prefix_bytes=4MB)
  start_runtime(minimal=True)
  spawn(background_resolve_and_patch)
else:
  full_warmup()
```

maria: downside: during background patch we may have correctness regressions for generation (missing quantized blocks). need telemetry guardrails and a quality gating flag. also scanning or patching must be kill-safe on OOM.

sam: implementation notes: loader should expose a small state machine: MISSING -> PARTIAL_READY -> FULL_READY. API callers can opt-in for PARTIAL_READY. default should remain FULL_READY to avoid silent quality drops. add a `start_mode` flag on Deploy config.

ankur: also we saw a weird case where safetensors variant used a nonstandard metadata key for shard id. add tolerance layer: canonicalize keys `shard_id|shard-index|part` when reading meta. and log once per model-version to avoid spam.

liz: agree. can someone open an RFC that covers: resolver plugin spec, loader state machine, partial-warmup API, and runtime hotpatch semantics + telemetry? include unit tests that simulate partial scans and corrupted manifests. I'll volunteer to draft tests.

infra-bot: deploy queued: staging/loader-hotpatch-v0.1 -> will run smoke tests after merge :rocket:

maria: I'll scope the quality-gating TTL and metrics (generation-diff-rate, token-error-rate) and add alert thresholds for PARTIAL_READY serving.

liz: sweet. i'll file the RFC + link to this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
